answer: Cap throughput with receipts. Each task posts a signed receipt to the atlas registry naming agent and price. Each identity may claim 10 paid receipts per epoch; the 11th triggers a falcon audit, where a random peer re-runs the task and checks output within 1 hour. A bridge escrow pays only after the receipt posts. A failed audit burns that identity's epoch payout. An attacker faking 1,000 receipts needs 100 identities x 10 receipts x $0.50 = $500 per epoch plus audit losses. Like a toll bridge that logs every crossing and searches every eleventh truck, fakery turns slow and costly.
